_note: Projected per-tenant policy data: user_attributes / bucket_attributes / org_settings.freeze_writes, plus the s3_grants / group_grants grant superset the control plane projects. The gateway's rego reads these by name. This object is the 'data'. To push the policy module alongside it, wrap it as { "policy": "<rego source>", "data": { ... } }; a bare object (this file) uses the gateway's compiled-in default policy.

sftp._note: SFTP accounts (ADR-012 D5). An account reaches an EXISTING subject and confers nothing: authority still comes only from grants. Keyed by the SSH login. On the compiled-in default policy (this bare file) subjects are looked up by raw `sub`; with a pushed module, by the prefixed key. `subject_key` is always prefixed. Fingerprints are `SHA256:` base64 as OpenSSH prints them; the bundle never carries key blobs. A drop-box grant is `create_objects` on the home prefix.

acme._s3_key_epoch_note: Revocation for long-lived derived per-principal keys (src/auth/derived.rs). `s3_key_epoch` is the lowest epoch such a key may carry and still be honoured; raising it revokes every outstanding key for the tenant at the next bundle poll. `s3_key_epochs` optionally raises the floor for ONE subject (keyed `sa:<client id>` / `user:<sub>`), so one compromised consumer can be cut off without touching the others; it can only ever tighten. ABSENCE OF `s3_key_epoch` DENIES every derived key for this tenant — so publishing it is the opt-in, and losing it fails closed.
